1

Why frame-level & multi-scale?

Playing techniques shape expressive violin performance, yet few detection models exist. VioTech labels three dimensions every 10 ms:

  • Note-level pipelines segment notes, then classify them; on violin, soft onsets and continuous bowing make segmentation unreliable, and errors cascade.
  • Frame-level prediction skips segmentation, but techniques are multi-scale: no single window fits all.
2

VioTech120 dataset

The first manually annotated violin technique dataset of real solo performances, with the first explicit legato (bow-change) labels.

120 étudesaligned audio–MIDI [5]multi-label2 violinists, peer-reviewed

Annotation interface (released)

Audio waveform with playback
MIDI piano roll aligned to audio, with legato spans
Per-note wheels: technique, articulation, string, position, finger

Fine-grained MIDI–audio alignment and temporal control; released to extend the dataset beyond techniques, e.g. fingering.

3

Multi-scale mixture-of-experts

Note-aware transcription cues and a frozen MERT encoder feed 8 temporal experts; a gating network per task routes them.

Temporal experts

Each expert learns its own weighting of the 25 MERT layers, then a dilated depthwise conv sets its window ki·di·10 ms, spaced exponentially from 20 ms to 2.56 s.

𝐡i′= ∑l=024 softmax(𝐰i)l ·𝐇l

Per-task gating & heads

𝐦task= ReLU(LayerNorm( ∑i αitask𝐞i ))
  • Tonal (3-way) & articulation (2-way): cross-entropy with focal loss + load balancing.
  • Legato: frame-wise regression to Gaussian targets at bow changes.
TrainVioTech120 + MOSA-VPT [1] (76 h synthetic, file-level labels) mixed 8 : 2 · 10 s segments · Adam, lr 5×10−4 Modeltranscription: HPT [4] as in VioPTT [1] · MERT-v1-330M [3], frozen · L = Ltrans + Ltech TestRWC [6] violin recordings (cross-dataset, unseen) · Bach10 & URMP for note transcription

How many experts?

MoE helps most on rare, expressive techniques, especially cross-dataset (3-seed means on RWC: pizzicato +32.8 pp, spiccato +15.5 pp), while near-ceiling classes barely move. The best expert count depends on technique and dataset.

6

What do the experts learn?

7

Take-home

  1. Frame-level, segmentation-free violin technique detection at 10 ms; new state of the art with strong cross-dataset generalisation.
  2. Experts specialise by time scale and MERT depth per technique, making the model interpretable; long-context experts for bow changes are next.
  3. VioTech120 + annotation interface released for violin technique and fingering research.
